To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the value of information of an amino acid increases in the course, of biological evolution.

the entropy of the amino-acids in the protein chain of the cytochrome c increases with the phylogenesis, and this is accompanied by the increase of the value (irreplaceability) of the information in the protein chain, i.e. with its evolution.
the entropy of a biological macromolecule increases in phylogenesis, which is accompanied by a decrease in its value of information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of the value of the information in the course of the evolution of the living organisms.
the problem of the origin of the biological information.
the evaluation of the relative probabilities of point mutations, with the notion of the value (irreplaceability) of information, and with the evaluation of its values in the proteins and RNA's.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the value of information increases with the increase of entropy of a protein.

the increase of the value and of the entropy is the result of the increase of the complexity of the protein chain in phylogenesis, and that the increase of entropy is the result not only of the increase of complexity but also of the decrease of redundancy.

the increase of the value (i.e. the irplaceability) of information in a protein chain is the result of the increase of the number of the point mutations, which are the result of the accumulation of the mutations during evolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the increase of the information value in the protein chains is a result of the increase of the number of point mutations in the course of phylogenesis.
the value of information increases in the process of biological evolution.
the value of information of the amino-accidic residues increases with the increase of their entropy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the information in the protein chains of the living organisms is organized in a very special way.
the value of information increases in the process of biological evolution and that the entropy and the value of the protein chains are correlated.
the information in proteins is not random, and it is not distributed evenly across the amino-acid residues.
